description: A graduate course on the methods that power modern deep learning, from the optimisation of deep networks to transformers, generative models, self-supervised learning, large-scale training, interpretability and deep reinforcement learning. Students implement and ablate each method at small scale, read recent papers critically and finish by reproducing a published result under a compute budget.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
Recent proceedings of the major machine learning conferences (reading list)
outcomes: Analyse the optimisation behaviour of deep networks and choose optimisers, schedules, initialisation and normalisation with justification.
Derive and implement the attention mechanism and the transformer, and explain its computational cost and efficient variants.
Derive the training objectives of VAEs, GANs and diffusion models and evaluate generated samples.
Apply self-supervised, contrastive and parameter-efficient methods to settings with scarce labels, such as low-resource African languages.
Estimate memory, compute and communication costs of distributed training and apply compression for deployment on constrained devices.
Critique a recent paper, design ablations with multiple seeds and report a reproduction honestly.

units.title: Optimisation of deep networks
topics: Loss landscapes: saddle points, sharp versus flat minima and mode connectivity
SGD, momentum and Nesterov acceleration; Adam and AdamW; learning-rate schedules and warm-up
Initialisation and normalisation: Xavier and He schemes, batch normalisation, layer normalisation, signal propagation
Residual connections and trainability; gradient clipping and exploding gradients
Generalisation: implicit regularisation, weight decay, dropout and double descent
Hyperparameter search, seeds and reproducible training runs

units.title: Attention and transformer architectures
topics: Sequence models revisited: recurrent networks, vanishing gradients, LSTM and GRU
Scaled dot-product and multi-head attention; sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings
The transformer encoder and decoder; masking, residual stream and feed-forward blocks
Pretraining objectives (causal and masked language modelling) and subword tokenisation including African languages
Vision transformers and multimodal models
Cost of attention: quadratic scaling, KV caching and efficient attention such as FlashAttention and sparse variants

units.title: Generative models: VAE, GAN and diffusion
topics: Latent variable models, the evidence lower bound and the VAE with the reparameterisation trick
Autoregressive and normalising-flow models as exact-likelihood generators
Generative adversarial networks: minimax objective, mode collapse and Wasserstein GAN
Diffusion models: forward noising, denoising score matching and DDPM sampling
Conditioning, classifier-free guidance and evaluating generators with FID, likelihood and human evaluation

units.title: Self-supervised and contrastive learning
topics: Pretext tasks and masked autoencoders
Contrastive objectives: InfoNCE, SimCLR and MoCo, and the mutual information bound
Non-contrastive methods such as BYOL and collapse avoidance
Transfer and fine-tuning: adapters, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods
Few-shot and low-resource learning for African languages and satellite imagery

units.title: Scaling, efficiency and distributed training
topics: Scaling laws and compute-optimal training
Data, tensor and pipeline parallelism; ZeRO sharding; the communication cost of all-reduce
Mixed precision, gradient checkpointing and memory accounting for parameters, activations and optimiser state
Compression: quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation for edge devices
Mixture-of-experts models and conditional computation
Cost, energy and carbon accounting of training and inference

units.title: Interpretability and robustness
topics: Attribution methods: saliency, integrated gradients, SHAP and sanity checks for explanations
Probing and mechanistic interpretability: circuits, attention heads and sparse autoencoders
Adversarial examples: FGSM, PGD, adversarial training and certified defences
Distribution shift, calibration and out-of-distribution detection
Safety evaluation, red teaming and failure analysis of deployed models

units.title: Deep reinforcement learning
topics: Markov decision processes recap; policy gradients, REINFORCE and baselines
Actor-critic methods: A2C and PPO with clipped objectives
Value-based deep RL: DQN, experience replay, target networks and double DQN
Continuous control with DDPG and SAC
Model-based and offline reinforcement learning; reinforcement learning from human feedback

units.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading and critiquing a recent paper: claims, evidence, baselines and ablations
Experiment tracking, seeds and statistical rigour in deep learning comparisons
Reproducing a published result under a fixed compute budget
Writing and presenting the reproduction report

schedule.title: Loss landscapes and optimisers
schedule.exercise: Derive the update rules of momentum and Adam, then explain in a page why AdamW decouples weight decay and when that matters.

tasks.title: Implement SGD, momentum and Adam from scratch and compare their loss curves on a two-layer network for the same learning-rate budget
Propagate activations through a 20-layer network under poor and He initialisation and watch the signal variance explode or vanish
Interpolate linearly between two trained solutions, plot the loss along the path and test whether a low-loss path connects them

schedule.title: Trainability and generalisation
schedule.exercise: Design a hyperparameter study for a small network with a fixed budget, and write the protocol you will follow to make the result reproducible.

tasks.title: Train networks of depth 10, 30 and 60 with and without residual connections and plot gradient norms per layer
Reproduce a double descent curve by fitting random-feature models of increasing width on a noisy regression task
Run a random search of 30 configurations with 3 seeds each and report which differences exceed seed noise

schedule.title: Sequence models and the attention mechanism
schedule.exercise: Derive scaled dot-product attention, explain the role of the square root of the key dimension and count the parameters of one transformer block.

tasks.title: Unroll an RNN over 50 steps, record the gradient magnitude per step and show the vanishing gradient, then repeat with an LSTM
Step single-head attention by hand on a 4-token sentence, showing scores, softmax weights and the weighted value sum
Implement a small decoder-only transformer with causal masking and train it on a character corpus to below 1.6 nats per character

schedule.title: Pretraining, tokenisation and efficient attention
schedule.exercise: Compare byte-pair encoding on English and on a Ghanaian language text sample and discuss what tokenisation costs low-resource languages.

tasks.title: Train a byte-pair tokenizer on a Twi or Ewe text sample and compare tokens per word with an English tokenizer
Patch an image into tokens, add position embeddings and verify the shape flow through a minimal vision transformer encoder
Measure attention time and memory against sequence length from 256 to 4,096, then add KV caching to autoregressive decoding and report the speed-up

schedule.title: Latent variable models and likelihood generators
schedule.exercise: Derive the evidence lower bound, show the two terms of the VAE loss and explain what posterior collapse is and how to avoid it.

tasks.title: Train a VAE on small digit images, plot the latent space and interpolate between two digits to inspect the decoder
Fit an autoregressive pixel model and a single-layer flow to the same 2D data and compare their log-likelihoods
Train a GAN on a 2D mixture of eight Gaussians, observe mode collapse and mitigate it with a Wasserstein loss

schedule.title: Diffusion models and evaluating generators
schedule.exercise: Compare VAE, GAN and diffusion models in a table covering sample quality, diversity, speed and training stability, with one citation per claim.

tasks.title: Implement the forward noising process and train a small denoiser on 2D data, then sample with DDPM and plot the trajectories
Apply classifier-free guidance at several scales on a conditional toy model and measure the trade-off between fidelity and diversity
Compute FID-style Frechet distance between real and generated feature sets for three generators and discuss when the metric misleads

schedule.title: Self-supervised, contrastive and efficient fine-tuning
schedule.exercise: Plan a pretraining and fine-tuning pipeline for a speech or text task in a low-resource African language, listing data, objective, compute and evaluation.

tasks.title: Pretrain a small masked autoencoder on unlabelled images, then train a linear probe and compare with training from scratch on 100 labels
Implement the InfoNCE loss with in-batch negatives, train with two augmentations and plot probe accuracy against batch size
Add LoRA adapters to a pretrained classifier, compare trainable parameter count and accuracy with full fine-tuning

schedule.title: Scaling laws and parallel training
schedule.exercise: Estimate memory and time for training a 1 billion parameter model on 8 GPUs, listing parameters, gradients, optimiser state and activations.

tasks.title: Fit a power law to loss against parameter count for five small models and extrapolate to predict loss at ten times the size
Simulate data, tensor and pipeline parallelism on a 4-device cluster and compare communication volume per step
Compute the memory budget of a transformer with and without mixed precision and checkpointing, then check your estimate against a measured run

schedule.title: Compression and efficient deployment
schedule.exercise: Write a deployment memo for running a language model on a low-cost phone with intermittent connectivity, justifying the compression choices you make.

tasks.title: Apply post-training 8-bit and 4-bit quantisation to a small model and report accuracy, size and latency at each precision
Route tokens through a four-expert mixture layer, show the load per expert and add a balancing loss to remove imbalance
Estimate energy and carbon cost of training and serving a model using given power and grid figures, and propose a cheaper schedule

schedule.title: Interpretability and robustness
schedule.exercise: Choose two interpretability methods and two robustness tests for a medical imaging classifier, and state what evidence would change your decision to deploy it.

tasks.title: Compute integrated gradients for a classifier and run a randomisation sanity check to see whether the attribution truly depends on the model
Craft FGSM and PGD adversarial images against a small CNN and measure robust accuracy before and after adversarial training
Detect out-of-distribution inputs with a max-softmax score and energy score, then report AUROC and calibration error under a covariate shift

schedule.title: Policy gradients and actor-critic
schedule.exercise: Derive the policy gradient theorem with a baseline and explain why the baseline lowers variance without adding bias.

tasks.title: Implement REINFORCE on a small control task, add a value baseline and compare the variance of the gradient estimates
Implement PPO with the clipped objective and plot returns for three clip ranges across five seeds
Train a DQN with experience replay and target network on a grid task and ablate each component to see the effect on stability

schedule.title: Continuous control, model-based and offline RL
schedule.exercise: Discuss in a short essay how reinforcement learning from human feedback differs from standard RL and what can go wrong with a learned reward.

tasks.title: Implement a soft actor-critic agent on a pendulum task and compare sample efficiency with a deterministic policy gradient baseline
Fit a learned dynamics model to logged transitions and plan with random shooting, comparing performance with a model-free agent
Train a reward model from 200 pairwise preferences and use it to fine-tune a small policy, then audit for reward hacking

schedule.title: Research methods and reproduction project
schedule.exercise: Submit a reproduction report: the claim, your setup, results with seeds and intervals, ablations, and an honest discussion of what did and did not reproduce.

tasks.title: Read a recent paper and write a structured critique listing its claims, baselines, missing ablations and threats to validity
Set up experiment tracking for a training script, run five seeds and report the mean and a bootstrap interval for the headline metric
Reproduce one table entry of a published result at reduced scale within a four-hour budget and explain every deviation
